races.name: Kilbeggan Irish Whiskey Maiden Hurdle

runners_data.name: Georg Zhukov
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning after a 96-day absence, all recent form in bumpers except one hurdle run; the step to 2m2½f on hurdles debut experience is fine on paper but this horse has zero placed hurdles form in similar going and faces a stiff ask fresh.|

runners_data.name: Hillhead Runner
runners_data.note: The confirmed pace-setter and form anchor of the race; trainer C Byrnes in 1/6 over 14 days and horse has 1 win and 4 places from 11 runs on similar going — a horse that knows its job and should face no rival for the lead, giving it a significant tactical advantage.|

runners_data.name: All Night Revival
runners_data.note: Consistent but winless hold-up/midfield type whose last five runs are littered with fourth-place finishes; the step up to 2m2½f suits on paper and Darragh O'Keeffe is a strong booking, but the horse needs a proper gallop to make up ground and may find the pace too controlled.|

runners_data.name: Chantilly Wings
runners_data.note: Returns after a 308-day absence — the longest layoff in the field — which is a significant fitness concern on quick ground; naturally a prominent racer who will find its customary position occupied by Hillhead Runner, forcing it to race out of its comfort zone on comeback day.|

runners_data.name: Codger's Rock
runners_data.note: Has a recent second on similar going (2/16f/GOO) suggesting current form, but by nature wants to race prominently and with Hillhead Runner in the way, Ben Harvey will need to decide quickly whether to contest the lead or drop in — its 0.93 style-fit tag reflects the compromise this creates.|

runners_data.name: Imarajan
runners_data.note: Paddy Cody (7) takes a 7lb claim which is useful at the weights; this horse has strong placed form in similar conditions (0W4P in 8 runs on similar going) and sits ideally positioned as a genuine prominent type who can get its natural spot just off Hillhead Runner's lead.|

runners_data.name: Penny Express
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott yard firing in form (6/44 over 14 days) and Penny Express has placed three times in nine runs on similar going; naturally hunts up near the pace and the trainer's current strike rate makes this a horse to respect as a stalker who could wear down the leader.|

runners_data.name: Urinmydreams
runners_data.note: Worrying profile — form string 8-0000, fades in finish tag, and holds the lowest rating in the field at OR 77; five consecutive poor runs on similar going (0W0P in 5) and a hold-up style in a race unlikely to have an honest enough gallop to bring that into play.|

races.paceDynamic: Hillhead Runner is the lone confirmed front-runner and, on Good to Firm ground at Kilbeggan over 2m2½f, will look to dictate from the front at a sustainable clip that suits a staying rhythm rather than a lung-busting gallop. With Codger's Rock and Chantilly Wings both naturally prominent types who are mapped to midfield due to congestion at the head of affairs, Hillhead Runner should enjoy an uncontested lead and control the tempo entirely on its own terms. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all occupy their preferred position — Hillhead Runner is most likely to secure the lead, with Codger's Rock and Chantilly Wings forced to race slightly further back than ideal. An uncontested, patient leader setting a true-but-not-punishing gallop on quick ground overwhelmingly favours horses that can travel close to the pace and quicken off it — prominent raiders and race-fit travellers who sit just behind the leader are best placed, while deep hold-up horses face too much ground to make up when the fractions are not honest enough to stretch the field.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Leader Controls, Kicks Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Hillhead Runner gets a clean lead and dictates an unchallenged, measured gallop throughout.
scenarios.body: Hillhead Runner settles into a rhythm with no rival willing to take it on, and the pace stays honest enough to be fair but not severe enough to expose stamina limits; the leader has the tactical advantage to quicken at the second-last and hold on. Horses sitting close to the pace — Imarajan and Penny Express — are best placed to latch on if the leader comes back to them late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Hillhead Runner's lead comes under challenge in the final mile and a prominent stalker presses and overtakes approaching the last.
scenarios.body: Imarajan or Penny Express, travelling smoothly just off the pace, applies pressure down the home straight and proves sharper than the tiring leader off the final hurdle. Good to Firm ground rewards economical jumping and a clean turn of foot, suiting a horse that has been produced with a run to give.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Finish Fast
scenarios.trigger: If Hillhead Runner sets a stronger-than-expected gallop that strings the field out and creates sufficient daylight for hold-up horses to close.
scenarios.body: Georg Zhukov or All Night Revival, held up off the pace, get a clear run from the home turn and pick off tiring rivals in the closing stages if the early tempo has been genuinely searching. This scenario is diminished by the likelihood that the pace will be controlled rather than punishing, limiting how much ground closers can make.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Market Drifter Upsets
scenarios.trigger: If the pace fragments, multiple errors are made at hurdles, and the race degenerates into a messy, slowly-run affair with a bunch finish.
scenarios.body: A muddling race with multiple stoppages or jumping errors can bring the whole field together for a sprint finish off a slow tempo, where lower-rated but fresh-legged horses like Codger's Rock or Chantilly Wings could sneak into contention. Urinmydreams' consistent poor form and finishing fade make it almost impossible to win under any scenario, but a genuinely chaotic race is the only context where an outsider could theoretically trouble the placed positions.

watchPoints.text: Hillhead Runner's jumping — if it makes a significant error at any of the early hurdles, it will lose the uncontested lead that underpins its entire chance and trigger a reshuffle of the entire race shape.

Chantilly Wings returning from 308 days off is a fitness wild card; if Carl Millar pushes forward early to get a prominent position, it could inject an unexpected pace injection that unsettles Hillhead Runner's rhythm.

Codger's Rock and Chantilly Wings may both attempt to press for prominent ground at the start, creating a brief early skirmish for position — watch how quickly that settles, as a scrappy first half-mile could compromise both horses' runs.

Imarajan's claim rider Paddy Cody (7lb) is worth monitoring in the market; if the horse is sharp at the start and gets a clean position just off Hillhead Runner, the weight advantage could be decisive in a tight finish.

Georg Zhukov's absence of 96 days — combined with a switch from bumpers to hurdles — means any drift in the market should be taken seriously, as trainer Eamonn O'Connell has sent just 0 winners from 2 runners over the past 14 days.

races.name: Writech Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Thecompanysergeant
runners_data.note: Confirmed pace-setter with Kilbeggan-relevant Good-ground wins; carries top weight of 166lbs and the STYLE_FIT tag means his chance diminishes if the prominent pack pushes him out of a comfortable lead, but if gifted daylight he is the primary danger.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out following a close second the run before, and already has today's distance under its belt. Sits third on our figures rather than top, but preferred here on the way that form is trending.

runners_data.name: Gameball
runners_data.note: Henry De Bromhead's six-year-old is unbeaten in two runs on Good ground and steps back up in trip having won at 16f; 71 days off is fine for this yard, and prominent style suits a Thecompanysergeant-led race perfectly.
runners_data.comment: Won two of the last four starts, with a third last time out extending a solid recent sequence. But our figures rate it modestly for this field at tenth, some way below the official mark, and it returns here after 71 days off.

runners_data.name: Bottler'secret
runners_data.note: 195-day absence is a significant concern; hold-up style leaves him dependent on a strong pace unwinding late, and his similar-going record (0W1P from five) offers little encouragement on this surface.
runners_data.comment: Rated the best in this field on our figures, well clear of the official mark, and already holds form over today's distance. The catch is 195 days off and a modest recent sequence — no better than fourth — leaving it without a win in that spell.

runners_data.name: Kamikaz Du Plessis
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's six-year-old has placed in nine of ten runs on similar going, and travelling prominent from gate makes him a consistent factor; the tongue-strap is retained, though a fall last time is worth noting.
runners_data.comment: Two thirds and a fourth feature in the past five starts, solid if unspectacular efforts, but it fell last time out and sits ninth on our figures for this field. Yet to score across that run despite the underlying consistency.

runners_data.name: Stede Bonnet
runners_data.note: Second Elliott runner and a natural prominent racer who has won twice this season; the switch to Good to Firm from softer ground is the question, but he is lightly weighted relative to recent wins and Danny Gilligan knows the horse.
runners_data.comment: Won twice in the past five starts, with a second last time out continuing a good recent thread, and has raced over today's distance previously. Sixth on our figures for this field, an unplaced effort two starts back the only real blemish.

runners_data.name: Grann's Boy
runners_data.note: Three wins and five places on all-ground form, but his Good-ground record specifically shows 11 from 15 — a concerning figure — and trainer H Rogers has had no winners in the last 14 days; seems to need easier conditions.
runners_data.comment: A win and a second feature among the last five starts, with experience over today's distance too. But form has tailed off since — ninth last time after an unplaced run — leaving fifth on our figures a fair reflection.

runners_data.name: Harry Des Ongrais
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old hold-up horse returning after 138 days, ridden by a 7lb claimer; no wins or places on similar going in four attempts, and the combination of absence and style make this a tough assignment.
runners_data.comment: Rated 12 lb above the official mark and second in this field on our figures, a striking gap. But the finishing figures are moderate, no better than third in the last four, and it returns from 138 days off winless in that spell.

runners_data.name: Ad Caelum
runners_data.note: Won over 24f on Good ground last time out and the 25-day turnaround for John Patrick Ryan is not unusual; Michael Kenneally's 5lb claim helps, and of the genuine hold-up types in this field Ad Caelum has the most relevant recent form.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out following a modest recent sequence, and is fairly fresh having last run just 25 days ago. But she sits only eleventh on our figures, in line with the official mark, so more is needed against this company.

runners_data.name: Gin Tonic
runners_data.note: Won on Good ground over 20f and placed over 24f; Paul Nolan's yard has had only three runners in 14 days but Gin Tonic's prominent style and 97 days' freshness could see him travel well — distance of this race marginally further than his best form.
runners_data.comment: A win and a second feature in the form book further back, but the last two starts have both ended in pulling up. Fourteenth on our figures for this field and returning after 97 days off, leaving plenty of questions.

runners_data.name: Lisnamult Lad
runners_data.note: A true prominent runner whose form cycle is dominated by P/0 finishes on Good ground; only six days since last run is aggressive freshness management, and the redistribution to midfield on the map reflects that he cannot realistically get his natural berth in this field — his 1W2P similar-going record at OR 118 is modest.
runners_data.comment: Rated 20 lb above the official mark and fourth in this field on our figures, a huge gap that marks it out. The finishing figures are poor, though — three pulled-up efforts among the last five — but it's fresh off a run just six days ago.

runners_data.name: Littlefoot
runners_data.note: Won twice over 20f including on soft, and headgear (tongue-strap) retained; travelling prominently at Kilbeggan suits, and the 56-day break for M A Molloy's yard looks straightforward — one of the likelier place prospects in the pack.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out, the second success in the past five starts, and already holds form over today's distance. Seventh on our figures for this field, with a pulled-up effort and a ninth further back in that sequence the blemishes.

runners_data.name: Paul's Dream
runners_data.note: Harry Cobden takes the ride for Anthony Mullins, which is an obvious angle; three wins on Good ground and a genuine front-running inclination means he will want to get forward — the redistribution note is honest: he may not secure that position in this field, and his best form has come at shorter trips.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out, backing up an earlier win in the same sequence, and she has experience over today's distance too. But our figures rate her only fifteenth for this field, a shade below the official mark, with a fall also in the mix.

runners_data.name: Nelson Muntz
runners_data.note: Hold-up profile on Good ground with a mixed record — best recent finish was 2nd over 16f but this 24f trip is significantly further; the blinkered headgear is retained and the 42-day break is unremarkable for David Harry Kelly.
runners_data.comment: A pair of thirds and a fourth feature among the last five starts, a reasonably tidy profile, and there's experience over today's distance too. But it's twelfth on our figures for this field and yet to score across that run.

runners_data.name: Faceman
runners_data.note: Consistent on Good ground (3W6P from 14 runs on similar), and Josh Williamson's 5lb claim is useful; his true front-running tendency is hemmed in by the field size, but he has placed consistently enough at this sort of distance to remain a factor if he salvages a prominent position.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out after a mixed run that included a fall, a fifth, a third and a fourth, so the form is patchy in isolation. Thirteenth on our figures for this field, meaning more is needed to build on that success against a stronger book.

runners_data.name: Rexem
runners_data.note: Returned just seven days ago and is asked to run again quickly; tongue-strip retained, and three places on Good ground suggest some ability, but the short turnaround on a sound surface and hold-up style mean he needs others to set it up.
runners_data.comment: Rated well above the official mark on our figures and fairly fresh, having last run just seven days ago, with a third last time the best of his recent runs bar a second further back. Yet to score in that run, and a pulled-up effort along the way is the concern.

runners_data.name: Ryan's Son
runners_data.note: Won at 16f on Good ground but all recent form is over shorter distances than today's 20f; a natural front-runner who will struggle to get his position in this 18-runner field, and Liz Doyle's yard has had only two runners in the past fortnight.
runners_data.comment: A win three starts back is the highlight of an otherwise modest recent sequence, with the last two outings both below par. Sixteenth on our figures for this field and back after 72 days off, leaving little to get excited about.

runners_data.name: Moon Mission
runners_data.note: Won over 18f on Good ground and finished fifth over 20f; P J Rothwell's yard has had one winner from 26 runners in the last 14 days, and this five-year-old has the engine but is another genuine front-runner who cannot realistically dominate from the front in this field.
runners_data.comment: A win figures among the last five, sandwiched by modest efforts either side, and a fifth last time did little to build on it. The yard is out of form too — just one winner from 26 in the past fortnight — compounding a lowly figure here.

runners_data.name: Has Me Dreaming
runners_data.note: 674 days off the track is the headline fact — both runs were on Good ground with wins and places, but returning from nearly two years' absence without a trainer 14-day strike rate to lean on makes this deeply speculative regardless of early speed.
runners_data.comment: Bounced back to win last time out having been third before that, but the form is buried in the past now — 674 days have elapsed since. Bottom of our figures for this field, that lengthy absence the obvious concern.

races.paceDynamic: Thecompanysergeant is the confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger likely to push him from the front, will dictate a controlled, single-file gallop from the off on Good to Firm ground at Kilbeggan. The apparent midfield cluster is deceptive — Lisnamult Lad, Paul's Dream, Faceman, Ryan's Son, Moon Mission and Has Me Dreaming are all natural front-runners or prominent racers who have been redistributed because the map cannot accommodate them all up close; in practice, several will jostle for early position and create more pressure on Thecompanysergeant than the headline shape suggests, though he remains the primary pace anchor. Gameball, Kamikaz Du Plessis, Stede Bonnet, Littlefoot and Gin Tonic are genuine prominent types who will track closely and are best placed to exploit the tempo being set. This race shape — a steady-to-honest pace set by one confirmed leader, with a genuine prominent pack immediately behind — strongly favours horses that can travel prominently, conserve energy through the middle, and produce a sustained run from the second-last hurdle, making prominent hold-a-position types the primary beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Pack Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Thecompanysergeant sets an honest but manageable gallop and the prominent horses immediately behind travel comfortably within themselves until the final turn.
scenarios.body: Gameball, Kamikaz Du Plessis and Stede Bonnet are ideally placed to track the pace and hit the front at the second-last; on Good to Firm ground with a fair weight of race behind them, those with strong similar-going form at this sort of trip will have the stamina to hold on.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Redistributed Runners Disrupt
scenarios.trigger: If the cluster of natural front-runners forced into midfield — Lisnamult Lad, Paul's Dream, Faceman — contest for early position and force a faster-than-expected early gallop.
scenarios.body: Thecompanysergeant faces more pressure than anticipated and the pace becomes strong enough to stretch the field, benefiting horses like Ad Caelum and Faceman who have shown they can finish powerfully when the race is truly run; Faceman's Good-ground form figures are consistent enough to merit respect even from a compromised draw.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Types Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the home straight and front-runners tie up, leaving ground for the true hold-up runners to sweep through.
scenarios.body: Ad Caelum won over this sort of trip on Good ground last time and is the most credible late finisher in the field; Nelson Muntz and Rexem can also pick up beaten horses if the race falls apart, though neither has the form figures to inspire confidence at the weights.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Bolts Up
scenarios.trigger: If Thecompanysergeant is left completely uncontested and the prominent pack misjudges the pace, giving him a soft lead at a canter throughout.
scenarios.body: At 135 OR and carrying 166lbs, Thecompanysergeant would need an unusually fortuitous race shape and rivals to fail to close, but his Good-ground win form and Gavin Cromwell's yard in fair recent form make this non-trivial; the style-fit discount applies but a true gift lead at Kilbeggan over this trip is dangerous.

watchPoints.text: Gameball and Stede Bonnet are both travelling with prominent profiles and strong similar-going form — if either gets a clean run through the first-last section and hits the front two out, the other runners may not have enough to peg them back.

Has Me Dreaming returns from 674 days off and, alongside Bottler'secret (195 days), may lack the fitness to jump safely in a strongly-run 18-runner hurdle on Good to Firm ground — monitor both in early stages for jumping errors.

The cluster of redistributed prominent types — Lisnamult Lad, Paul's Dream, Faceman, Ryan's Son, Moon Mission — will jostle for position in the first half-mile; watch for crowding or interference near the early hurdles as they compete for the same ground.

Ad Caelum is the only genuine hold-up horse with a recent win over this sort of trip on Good ground; if the pace collapses in the home straight rather than staying honest, he is the one hold-up runner whose profile genuinely fits that scenario.

Thecompanysergeant's 166lb burden is the highest weight in the race by margin — if the pace becomes contested and he is forced to quicken earlier than planned, watch for him to shorten in the final half-mile, which would hand the race to the prominent pack behind.

races.name: Kilmurray Group Midlands National Handicap Chase (Listed)

runners_data.name: Amirite
runners_data.note: Confirmed pace-setter and only true front-runner in the race; ten-year-old has shown she can control from the front at 3m+ on good ground (won 26f on Good), but a 90-day layoff for De Bromhead and a style-fit flag mean she may not dominate as cleanly as her position suggests.|
runners_data.comment: A win earlier in a promising spell that also yielded a fourth marks him a clear leader in this field on our figures, and he has run over today's distance before. Two pulled-up efforts since are the obvious reservation, but there is enough in the book to take on trust after a break.

runners_data.name: Perceval Legallois
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old for Cromwell who has won on good and shown placed form at this grade, though recent form includes several pulled-up efforts and his best similar-going figures (1W2P from 6 runs) are workmanlike rather than standout; 46 days since last run is fine.|
runners_data.comment: A close second on our figures and clearly capable on his day, with a fourth figuring among the past five starts. Conduct has been the issue though, with two pulled-up efforts and one unseated in that sequence leaving him without a win to show for it.

runners_data.name: Uncle Pat
runners_data.note: Townend in the saddle for Mullins is a strong angle, and the horse's record on similar going is excellent (3W5P from 9 runs); placed efforts at 28-32f on soft/heavy suggest the step up in trip on a quicker surface genuinely suits, making him a prime candidate to secure a prominent pitch.|
runners_data.comment: Ended a sequence of three seconds and an unseated with a win last time and has form over today's trip, so the profile is workmanlike. Only mid-pack on our figures for this line-up, though, leaving that recent success to carry plenty of weight if replicated.

runners_data.name: Native Speaker
runners_data.note: Won last time out over 24f on Good for De Bromhead and has consistent form at this course-going combination (3W6P from 10 runs); races prominently and Darragh O'Keeffe is well-placed to slot him in just off Amirite.|
runners_data.comment: Bounced back to win last time after a run of finishes down the field (9th, 8th, 7th before that), and has raced over today's trip previously. Sits mid-pack on our figures for this field, so more needed to confirm that turnaround against a stronger line-up.

runners_data.name: Boston Rover
runners_data.note: Lightly raced seven-year-old who won three on the spin on good ground earlier in career, but has been absent 264 days and returns for Elliott with only a P to his name last time; if fit, his similar-going stats (3W5P) are excellent and he could be very dangerous at the price.|
runners_data.comment: Boasted a productive streak of three wins from four before pulling up last time, form that reads well in isolation. But a spell of 264 days off the track and a fringe rating for this field make him hard to trust fully back.

runners_data.name: Olympic Man
runners_data.note: Consistent finisher in minor positions rather than a winner at this level; similar-going record shows just one placed effort from 7 runs, and a headgear note (tp) has not unlocked improvement; amateur jockey Doyle also a disadvantage in this company.|
runners_data.comment: Rated well above the official mark and third in the field on our figures, plenty of encouragement despite a modest profile. But the form's messy — a fall and two pulled-ups among the last five — leaving it winless in that sequence.

runners_data.name: Solitary Man
runners_data.note: Bolger-trained eight-year-old with a fine similar-going record (3W6P from 10 runs); won over 23f on Good recently and has the profile of a horse who travels prominently and stays well — could benefit if Amirite cuts back the pace.|
runners_data.comment: Two wins feature among the last five starts, with a fourth last time out and experience over today's distance already banked. Ranks fourth on our figures for this field, a below-par ninth earlier in that sequence the only obvious blot.

runners_data.name: Raglan Road
runners_data.note: Won over 25f on Good last time out for De Bromhead with Cobden, who travels from Britain — a strong booking; naturally prominent but the field congestion means he may not secure that position, and racing off the pace he loses some of his edge.|
runners_data.comment: Returned to winning form last time out, backing up an earlier win in the same sequence, and has raced over today's distance before. Only mid-table on our figures for this field though, with a pulled-up effort and two finishes down the field also in the mix.

runners_data.name: Drumgill
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old whose recent form string (5-7-U-7-5) reflects inconsistency; a natural front-runner who will be squeezed into a midfield role he does not relish given the numbers ahead of him, and the 25-day turnaround is brisk.|
runners_data.comment: Sits above the official mark on our figures and is fairly fresh, having last run just 25 days ago, with a fifth the pick of a middling recent sequence. Yet to score in that spell, and an unseated effort along the way is the concern.

runners_data.name: Pride Of Place
runners_data.note: Won over 26f on Good last season and Bolger has form with this type, but has since pulled up in a handicap and the blinkers are fitted; competes prominently in style yet will be pushed back into a tracking role, which dilutes his chance.|
runners_data.comment: Anchors our figures for this field, with a modest recent sequence — 9th, 9th and 8th figuring alongside a win two starts back before pulling up last time out. Hard to fancy from bottom of the pile on this book, in spite of that one bright spot.

runners_data.name: Yoradreamer
runners_data.note: Mullins runner who finished second last time on Good and has placed form at this trip in similar conditions; a genuine prominent type forced into a deeper role by the numbers — his best chance depends on the front group coming back to him.|
runners_data.comment: Down near the foot of our figures for this field, though a second last time out was a fair effort and a win figures three starts back. An unseated performance in between clouds the picture, and more consistency is needed to threaten up here.

runners_data.name: Shanbally Kid
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator noted as prone to fading in the finish, and a record of P-4-P-U-P in recent outings is not encouraging; the Mullins yard is in form (T14: 14/116) but this horse's own form makes him a risky closer even if the pace falls apart.|
runners_data.comment: Rated well clear of the official mark and fifth in this field on our figures, a striking gap given the profile. But the results have been miserable — three pulled-up efforts and an unseated among the last five — leaving it without a win to show.

runners_data.name: Will Do
runners_data.note: Elliott runner whose form reads 0-P-0-P-P and whose similar-going record is thin (1 placed from 4); blinkers fitted but has not found his form and will struggle racing further from the pace than he'd like.|
runners_data.comment: Sits well clear of the official mark on our figures at seventh in this field, but the form book makes for tough reading with three pulled-up efforts and two unplaced finishes across the last five starts, leaving it winless throughout.

runners_data.name: Invictus Machin
runners_data.note: Cromwell's second runner alongside Perceval Legallois, fitted with a hood and with placed form on similar going (1W3P); naturally prominent but slotted into a midfield role — Mark Walsh's experience may help him find an opening, but the position shuffle is a genuine disadvantage.|
runners_data.comment: A fourth and two seconds feature in the recent form, evidence of ability, but it pulled up last time out and sits only twelfth on our figures for this field. Yet to score across that sequence despite the underlying consistency.

runners_data.name: Lonesome Boatman
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old with a win on Good over 28f in his record (1W3P from 7 similar-going runs) and a 129-day break; runs without a jockey listed in the data which is a concern, and the long absence plus the redistribution to midfield combine to dilute any residual appeal.|
runners_data.comment: Some ability on show with a win and a third figuring in the past five, but pulled up last time out and has had a lengthy 129-day absence since. Only thirteenth on our figures for this field, leaving plenty to prove fresh off that lay-off.

runners_data.name: Moonovercloon
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with 13 runs on similar going producing only 2 placed efforts from 13 — a persistence record that rarely translates to success; the visor is fitted and he has been running in shorter-trip races, making the 3m1½f a stamina question.|
runners_data.comment: Second from bottom of our figures for this field, with the recent form modest throughout — no better than a fourth in the last five starts, and three finishes worse than sixth. Remains without a win across that sequence too.

runners_data.name: A Penny A Hundred
runners_data.note: Mullins hold-up runner who has placed form on Good ground (1W4P from 10 similar-going runs); recent form has tailed off (7-4-7-0-3) and at the bottom of the weights the trip looks a stretch given his last five have all been at shorter distances.|
runners_data.comment: Rated well above the official mark on our figures, sitting ninth in this field despite a recent run of finishes worse than midfield, including two seventh-place efforts. Without a win across that sequence, she needs the uplift in the book to be right.

races.paceDynamic: Amirite is the one confirmed front-runner here and, with a clear path from the front, can control a genuine but manageable gallop over 3m1½f on Good to Firm at Kilbeggan — sustainable enough that she will not burn herself out, but fast enough to stretch the field early. The redistribution note is critical: Raglan Road, Pride Of Place, Yoradreamer, Will Do, Drumgill, Invictus Machin and Lonesome Boatman are all natural prominent-racing types who cannot all hold those positions simultaneously, meaning several will be shuffled wider and deeper than ideal, creating a compressed midfield bunch who will be racing partially out of role. Uncle Pat, Native Speaker, Boston Rover, Solitary Man and Perceval Legallois are the horses most likely to actually secure the prominent positions just off Amirite, with the redistributed horses forming a contested and fractious mid-group. The race shape strongly favours horses who can travel fluidly in the first three to five positions without expending energy fighting for ground — genuine prominent types with good jumping records and the stamina to see out the trip on quick ground benefit most here.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Amirite dictates at a measured pace and one of the genuine prominent horses tracks her comfortably before asserting from the last.
scenarios.body: Amirite sets fractions that suit herself and the horses travelling efficiently in second and third, with the chasing pack expending energy fighting for position; the horse who jumps cleanly from the front group and quickens off the bend wins going away.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Closer Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Amirite goes too fast for the conditions and weakens from three out, allowing a hold-up horse or deep midfield runner to pick up the pieces.
scenarios.body: A faltering gallop from the front creates a bunched finish turning in, and a horse who has been produced patiently from off the pace benefits from rivals having done too much earlier; the closing surge is brief but decisive on Good to Firm ground.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Scrap, Attrition Wins
scenarios.trigger: If several of the redistributed prominent types fight for position early and the pace becomes ragged and hard-run, favouring a stayer who grinds them down.
scenarios.body: Multiple horses racing out of role create carnage from the mid-stages onwards as stamina reserves are drained by the scrapping; the horse with the deepest reserves and cleanest jumping record survives the chaos.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Storms Home
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong throughout and the prominent group all tie up from two out, giving a true hold-up runner a clear late run.
scenarios.body: Shanbally Kid or A Penny A Hundred get a clean passage on the outer as the leaders weaken, but the finishing straight at Kilbeggan is short and this scenario requires near-perfect execution; the form of both horses in this grade is modest.

watchPoints.text: Boston Rover has a 264-day layoff to overcome for Elliott but arrives with a three-timer on good ground on his CV and could be dangerously fresh if spot-on — watch his jumping in the early stages for signs of rustiness or sharpness.

The redistribution crunch between Raglan Road, Pride Of Place, Yoradreamer and Drumgill for limited prominent positions is a genuine flashpoint — if two or more of them clash for the same ground at the first fence, expect scrimmaging that could unsettle others and bring down the early pace.

Amirite's 90-day layoff for a ten-year-old front-runner is worth monitoring in the paddock and the early stages — if she jumps out flat or is not travelling fluidly by the third fence, the shape of the whole race collapses.

Uncle Pat's jumping will be critical: Townend can place him perfectly in second or third, but an error at one of Kilbeggan's tight-turn fences from a horse stepping up to 3m1½f on quick ground could cost him all chance.

Good to Firm conditions throughout the card at Kilbeggan favour quick-jumping, prominent types with sound limbs — any runner whose trainer has flagged ground preference for soft (notably Perceval Legallois and Shanbally Kid, whose best form comes on soft/heavy) should be treated with caution at these conditions.

races.name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Beginners Chase

runners_data.name: Centreofattention
runners_data.note: Inconsistent recent form (/670-8) and 56 days off the track; a true hold-up performer whose natural rear-of-field role is compromised in this race because the back positions are over-subscribed, and similar-going form reads 0 wins from 6.
runners_data.comment: Yet to threaten in recent starts, with finishes no better than sixth across the last four and an eighth last time out the poorest of them. Sixth on our figures for this smaller field, and clearly workmanlike.

runners_data.name: Charlie Luciano
runners_data.note: Noel Meade runner fresh off 40 days rest with form figures PP0P-4 suggesting stamina and jumping are live questions; genuinely wants to come from the back but the hold-up berths are congested here, leaving him exposed in a midfield role that isn't his comfort zone.
runners_data.comment: Rated above the official mark on our figures and third in this smaller field, with a fourth last time out the highlight of a stop-start sequence. Three pulled-up efforts elsewhere in that run leave it without a win to show, the obvious knock.

runners_data.name: Franciscan Rock
runners_data.note: Highest official rating in the field at OR 136 and trained by Mouse Morris whose 14-day record shows 1/1; however his last five runs include an absence of 71 days and form (49527) on good ground is unconvincing despite a place record in softer conditions.
runners_data.comment: Clear at the top of our figures for this smaller field, with a second the standout effort among the last five. Yet to score in that sequence and it's had 71 days off, but the underlying quality marks it out as the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Juke Hill
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott second-string alongside Scalpnagoon, fitted with a hood and just 10 days since last run; a hold-up horse whose good-ground form reads 0 wins and 1 place from 6, and the step up to 3m1½f is a question mark against his profile.
runners_data.comment: Bottom of our figures for this field, and the recent form does little to argue against it — finishes no better than fourth across the last five starts. Freshened by a run just ten days ago, but yet to score throughout that sequence.

runners_data.name: Kevin's Pride
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed pace-setter, handled by JJ Slevin and OR 119; won over 2m on good and placed multiple times at this trip, making him structurally central to every scenario — his jumping fluency from fence to fence will define the race shape entirely.
runners_data.comment: A win and a second feature among the last four, though the two starts since have been modest. The yard is out of form too — just one winner from 20 in the past fortnight — leaving fifth on our figures a fair snapshot.

runners_data.name: Orkneys Jack
runners_data.note: Ridden by a 7lb claimer and flagged as a horse who fades in the finish; form (82-513) shows a win and place at shorter trips but the 3m1½f distance combined with the fade tendency makes the closing stages a serious concern.
runners_data.comment: A win two starts back is the highlight of a mixed recent sequence that also features a couple of finishes down the field. Seventh on our figures for this smaller field, with a third last time out at least a step forward.

runners_data.name: Scalpnagoon
runners_data.note: Second Elliott runner, consistent form figures (3-2234) with 9 places from 13 on similar ground and a tongue-tie fitted; 10 days since last run and prominently raced, meaning he is ideally positioned to track Kevin's Pride and challenge from two out.
runners_data.comment: A model of consistency of late, with two seconds and two thirds figuring among the last five and a fourth last time out the only finish outside the frame. Fourth on our figures for this field, still without a win despite that reliability.

runners_data.name: Tonaghneave Well
runners_data.note: Gavin Cromwell's runner holds a strong 14-day trainer strike rate (7/55) but recent form (669-89) and a hood suggest he is struggling for consistency; prominent in his races, he sets up well tactically but needs to rediscover better form to be a winning factor.
runners_data.comment: Rated above the official mark on our figures and runner-up in this field's pecking order, a notable gap given the profile. The finishing figures are poor though — nothing better than sixth across the last five — leaving it without a win to show for that placing.

races.paceDynamic: Kevin's Pride is the lone confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine rival to press him, JJ Slevin can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop over this 3m1½f trip on Good to Firm ground at Kilbeggan. Scalpnagoon and Tonaghneave Well will track prominently just off Kevin's Pride, creating a compact early order, while the field's hold-up contingent — Franciscan Rock, Juke Hill, Centreofattention, and Charlie Luciano — will be strung out behind. The field carries more hold-up horses than the map can honestly accommodate at the rear; Centreofattention and Charlie Luciano are true come-from-behind types who have been redistributed to midfield because natural rear positions are over-subscribed, meaning they are unlikely to get the ground-saving trip their style ideally demands. With Kevin's Pride able to bowl along uncontested and set a fair but manageable tempo, this race shape strongly favours prominent-raced horses with the stamina to grind home — horses who can travel in the slipstream of the leader without burning fuel, then pick off a tiring pace-setter in the final circuit.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Kevin's Pride Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Kevin's Pride bowls along unchallenged and the pace is honest without being brutal, prominent stalkers who travel smoothly off him inherit the race.
scenarios.body: Kevin's Pride sets a metronomic gallop and Scalpnagoon or Tonaghneave Well sit in the perfect position to challenge two out, with the race becoming a staying test from the second-last; horses who have raced prominently all season and handle Good to Firm ground have every structural advantage here.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Kevin's Pride slightly over-extends in front and a prominent tracker conserves enough energy to overhaul him between the last two fences.
scenarios.body: Scalpnagoon's consistent form figures (2234) and course-distance suitability make him the chief beneficiary if he can sit a length off the leader and produce a clean round; Tonaghneave Well offers a similar profile but his recent form (89) is less convincing on this faster surface.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Rally From Deep
scenarios.trigger: If the early gallop is genuinely strong and the prominent horses stop, allowing a hold-up horse to close through beaten rivals on the run-in.
scenarios.body: Franciscan Rock is the highest-rated runner in the field at OR 136 and possesses the class to finish powerfully if the pace burns others off, though his recent form figures (49527) and trainer's sparse 14-day record offer little confidence; Juke Hill is fresh (10 days) and wore a hood, but his staying form has been inconsistent.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos, Errors And Attrition
scenarios.trigger: If the beginners' chase nature of the race produces jumping errors and fallers that reshuffle the order entirely.
scenarios.body: In a field of novice chasers over 3m1½f, accumulated jumping mistakes can eliminate market leaders and hand the race to a safe, economical jumper who simply stays upright; Orkneys Jack's fade warning means he'd need a reduced field to capitalise, but Kevin's Pride's jumping efficiency on the day becomes critical.

watchPoints.text: Kevin's Pride — watch his jumping from the outset; as the lone front-runner in a beginners' chase, any jumping error or hesitation at a fence will immediately compress the field and gift prominent rivals like Scalpnagoon a free passage to the lead.

Orkneys Jack — flagged as a horse who fades in the finish and partnered by a 7lb claimer; watch for him travelling prominently through the early stages and then weakening sharply from the third-last, potentially causing interference with those making late runs.

Centreofattention and Charlie Luciano — both true hold-up horses forced into midfield by overcrowding at the rear; watch whether they drift wider than ideal looking for a run, burning extra energy on a Good to Firm surface over 3m1½f.

Franciscan Rock — highest-rated horse and absent 71 days; watch in the preliminary paddock inspection for signs of fitness and then in the early fences for jumping fluency, as a novice chaser returning from a break over this trip can be fragile in the opening mile.

races.name: Larrigy's Pub Handicap Hurdle (0-100)

runners_data.name: Goin'
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse from A J Martin's yard returning in 33 days; has placed twice in similar going but fades in finishes, and with so many genuine closers crowding the rear this field shape does not favour its natural style.
runners_data.comment: Goin' arrives on modest recent form — 5th, two unplaced runs and a 9th in his last four starts, still without a win in that time. He has raced over today's distance before, and a rating of 96 keeps him around midfield here.

runners_data.name: Backwithyourown
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner and key pace-setter; trained by John M Burke who is 0/2 in the last 14 days, and the STYLE_FIT flag warns it is racing out of its most effective role — yet it will get the lead by default and that lead is an asset in itself.
runners_data.comment: Backwithyourown was runner-up three starts back and has generally raced creditably, though she remains without a win and was unseated last time out. She has raced over today's distance before, and a rating of 97 keeps her well involved in this field.

runners_data.name: Kentucky Bluebird
runners_data.note: Hold-up type from Gavin Cromwell's yard, who is only 1/31 in the last 14 days; has failed to place in 5 recent starts on similar going and looks to have a difficult draw on form alone.
runners_data.comment: Kentucky Bluebird has been held up in a run of modest finishes, no better than 4th in her last five starts and still without a win. Her trainer is currently out of form, and a rating of 89 leaves her needing more to threaten from midfield.

runners_data.name: Scathach
runners_data.note: Versatile runner (style unknown) from Ross O'Sullivan who has been in strong form at 4/20 over 14 days; placed once in similar going, and Danny Gilligan aboard could help secure a good position early in a race that suits handy types.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out is the one bright spot for the mare, but the surrounding form is poor — a fall in the mix and nothing else better than sixth, still without a win. She has raced over today's distance before, though our 82 rating leaves her towards the bottom of this field.

runners_data.name: Bowgate Street
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up performer wearing a tongue-tie; won over this C&D trip at 1/18f on good ground and Darragh O'Keeffe is a significant booking, though the horse fades in finishes and the crowded hold-up group makes late delivery trickier.
runners_data.comment: She landed a win in the middle of her recent form, with a third close by, but has tailed off since — beaten into 8th and then unplaced last time. Proven over today's distance, our 88 rating keeps her among the pack.

runners_data.name: Georginas Jet
runners_data.note: Prominent-style runner racing just 6 days after a run — freshness must be assessed — but has a win at 18f on good ground and sits in a position in this race shape that suits a controlled gallop; Jack Gilligan's 5lb claim helps the weight.
runners_data.comment: Georginas Jet landed one two starts back and followed up with a 4th last time out, a turnaround after two pulled-up efforts further back. She has raced over today's distance before, but a rating of 86 leaves her hard to fancy as an outsider.

runners_data.name: Notmiwadi
runners_data.note: Returning from 284 days off, a serious absence flag; this true hold-up horse has been mapped to midfield because the rear is overcrowded, and its pattern of fading in finishes combined with a long layoff makes its chance hard to frame confidently.
runners_data.comment: Notmiwadi has managed nothing better than 7th in her last four starts and is winless throughout, out of the weights on our figures at 72. A long absence of 284 days doesn't help, though she has raced over today's distance before.

runners_data.name: Vairue
runners_data.note: Off the track for 589 days — the longest layoff in the field — and has a finish-fading pattern; won once on good ground at 16f but the extended absence and true hold-up style in an unfavourable race shape are significant negatives.
runners_data.comment: Vairue returns after 589 days off the track, his last four starts yielding nothing better than a 4th and still without a win. Fitness is the obvious question after such a lengthy absence, though a rating of 88 keeps him in the pack.

runners_data.name: Monty's Way
runners_data.note: An 8-year-old veteran who genuinely likes to come from the rear, but the field density forces it towards midfield on the map; headgear (tongue-piece) and one win on good ground at 18f noted, though recent form reads 0-0-0 at this trip.
runners_data.comment: On our figures he rates strongly at 100 — third-best in this field and well clear of his official 84 — and he has raced over today's distance before, so the raw ability marks him a danger. The obvious risk is a patchy recent profile: a pulled-up run in the mix and unplaced in each of his last two starts, still without a win.

runners_data.name: Boston Bobby
runners_data.note: Won at 17f on good ground from a hold-up position, but has been wearing a hood and is a true rear-of-field horse pushed forward on the map by overcrowding; recent sixth from a field of similar quality doesn't inspire confidence.
runners_data.comment: Boston Bobby landed one three starts back but the two starts since have been modest, beaten into 6th last time out having also finished unplaced. He has raced over today's distance before, though a rating of 81 leaves him towards the rear of this field.

runners_data.name: Granlahan
runners_data.note: Prominent-style 4-year-old lightly raced and racing just 6 days after a run; has placed twice at 18-20f and Adrian McGuinness has been active (2/28 in 14 days), so there is enough residual form to suggest it can sit close enough to benefit from this pace shape.
runners_data.comment: Granlahan was twice third in the middle of his last five starts but is without a win in that time and unseated when last seen. He has raced over today's distance before and a rating of 89 keeps him firmly in the pack.

runners_data.name: Maybe Someday
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up type mapped to midfield by necessity; has headgear (tongue-piece and blinkers) and a 25-day turnaround, but the fading pattern and zero wins or places on this going in 5 attempts makes it hard to support.
runners_data.comment: The bare form is patchy — a fourth last time her best of a run that includes several unplaced efforts and a fifth — yet she rates fourth in this field on our figures at 98, well above her official 80. That figure marks her a live danger if she can run to it, though she is yet to win.

runners_data.name: Not So Serious
runners_data.note: True rear-of-field horse displaced forward on the map due to the overcrowded hold-up group; two pulled-ups in recent form and zero finishes in the top 12 on similar going in 5 attempts — Anna McGuinness on a 7lb claim does little to mitigate a poor form profile.
runners_data.comment: Not So Serious has raced over today's distance before, and despite a moderate recent line — pulled up twice among three unplaced efforts — he heads our figures on 106, well clear of his official mark of 80. That gain on our numbers is what puts him on top.

runners_data.name: Gold Gatewood
runners_data.note: Off the track for 409 days; the tongue-tie is new but the sparse form line (only 3 runs on similar going) makes it hard to evaluate, and J J Slevin is a strong booking that adds minimal optimism for a horse returning from near-14 months off.
runners_data.comment: Gold Gatewood remains unexposed with only three starts under his belt, unplaced last time out over 409 days ago after a spell that also included an 8th and a pulled-up run. The sample is limited, leaving room for improvement as he returns to the track.

runners_data.name: Wings Of Africa
runners_data.note: Five-year-old with a string of pulled-ups and zeros; the three pieces of comparable going form have returned modest placings at best and the fading pattern combined with redistribution to midfield means this true hold-up type has structural disadvantage.
runners_data.comment: Wings Of Africa remains lightly raced, a 6th last time out following two pulled-up efforts sandwiched by unplaced runs in her last five starts. The book is limited so far, leaving scope for improvement as she gains more experience.

runners_data.name: Chesterbaylad
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse in a field where true closers are disadvantaged by the pace map; Josh Younge's 7lb claim is noted, but the form — including a 17th on similar going — and the structural positioning issues make it hard to see a route to victory.
runners_data.comment: Chesterbaylad was runner-up two starts back but could only manage 7th last time out, with two unplaced efforts and a 9th further back in his recent form. Still without a win in that spell, a rating of 83 leaves him towards the lower end of this field.

runners_data.name: High Notions
runners_data.note: Top-rated at OR=99 and the class flag of the race; hold-up style but has one win from 8 runs on similar going and placed twice, and if the pace collapses late this is the one with enough raw ability to charge through from midfield — note no jockey listed which is a query.
runners_data.comment: High Notions has raced over today's distance before and rates second in the field at 103, above her official mark of 99. Third two starts back, she could only manage 7th last time out, with modest efforts further back — fitness the main query.

runners_data.name: Glendine Billy
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old hold-up horse from Anthony Mullins, running just 7 days after a start; consistent pattern of finishing 8th-10th in comparable good-ground races, and there is nothing in the form to suggest this moderate run of placings will be broken here.
runners_data.comment: Glendine Billy has struggled for form of late, no better than 8th and including a pulled-up effort in his last four starts, still winless in that time. A quick reappearance just seven days on keeps him fresh, and a rating of 93 holds him around midfield.

runners_data.name: Annarubyrose
runners_data.note: Prominent-style runner from Ian Patrick Donoghue who is 2/17 in 14 days; has placed twice at 22f on good ground and loves this trip — sitting handy is a genuine asset in a race with only one pace-setter, and this is one of the horses best served by the race shape.
runners_data.comment: A mixed profile — a runner-up effort is the pick of it, with a third at the far end of her last five and a couple of well-beaten runs in between, still without a win. She has raced over today's distance before and our 89 rating keeps her firmly in the pack.

races.paceDynamic: Backwithyourown is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 19-runner field and is likely to stride into an uncontested lead from the front, setting a sustainable rather than pressured gallop over 2m2½f on Good to Firm ground at Kilbeggan. With no genuine challenger for the lead, Backwithyourown can control tempo entirely, which on a track that rewards horses travelling comfortably close to the pace makes prominent and handy racers the primary beneficiaries. The field is loaded with natural hold-up types — Notmiwadi, Monty's Way, Boston Bobby, Maybe Someday, Not So Serious and Gold Gatewood among others are true rear-of-field horses who have been mapped to midfield purely because there is no room for them all at the back; in reality, many will find themselves further back than ideal. With one genuine pace-setter dictating an honest but unforced gallop, prominent and handy racers such as Georginas Jet, Annarubyrose and Granlahan are best positioned to exploit this race shape, with hold-up horses carrying a structural disadvantage in a race where the tempo is unlikely to be strong enough to bring them into play late.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Backwithyourown dictates an uncontested, measured gallop and the pace is never truly pressured.
scenarios.body: Backwithyourown bowls along in front setting a comfortable fractions, allowing prominent racers sitting just behind to travel in a rhythm and pounce from the second-last; horses that get a clear run from handy positions will have first run on any hold-up types.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Outstays Field
scenarios.trigger: If Backwithyourown's control of pace is so complete that the field strings out and it simply is never headed.
scenarios.body: Racing on Good to Firm ground which rewards a slick jumper travelling sweetly, Backwithyourown potentially posts a wire-to-wire success if those behind it use up energy trying to close gaps that never fully materialise; this scenario rewards horses with strong jumping and front-running efficiency.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Surge From Midfield
scenarios.trigger: If the early gallop is faster than expected and several prominent horses tire approaching the last, creating a gap for horses travelling through the field.
scenarios.body: A stronger-than-anticipated pace would compress the finishing positions and allow a well-handicapped hold-up type who avoids traffic problems to pick up ground; given Good to Firm conditions and 19 runners, the risk of being blocked is real and only the cleanest-travelling closer can capitalise.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Race Falls Apart, Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If there are early fallers, unseats or interference that disrupt race order and create a messy, uneven gallop.
scenarios.body: In a 19-runner handicap hurdle on a tight track, disruption to the pace structure could create a stop-start tempo where adaptable horses with strong jumping and a versatile style come to the fore; runners with cleaner recent form and experienced jockeys navigating the chaos are best placed.

watchPoints.text: Backwithyourown will go straight to the front unchallenged — watch whether Eoin Walsh settles it or allows it to bowl along, as this tempo decision shapes the entire race outcome.
Georginas Jet and Annarubyrose are the two prominent types best positioned to exploit a controlled gallop — if either gets a clean passage from the second-last they are the primary threat.

With 19 runners at Kilbeggan over 2m2½f, early jumping errors or fallers at the first few flights could cause significant interference — Gold Gatewood (409-day layoff) and Notmiwadi (284 days off) are the two most likely to be rusty at the obstacles.
High Notions carries top weight at OR=99 and no jockey is listed — confirm the rider before the race as a headline jockey booking could significantly alter its market position and tactical approach.

The genuine hold-up horses (Boston Bobby, Monty's Way, Maybe Someday, Not So Serious, Wings Of Africa) are all mapped forward by necessity but will likely drop to the rear naturally — watch for a logjam of closers with nowhere to go if the pace is only moderate.

races.name: New Forest Estate & Golf Club Handicap Hurdle (0-100)

runners_data.name: Down Around
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner at OR 98 for P J Rothwell, last run 232 days ago; good-to-firm form reads 13/15 with a win and four places, so conditions suit, but the STYLE_FIT flag notes it is technically out of its ideal role in this shape — primary value is in what it creates rather than what it wins.
runners_data.comment: Down Around heads our figures clearly on 110 — well above his official mark of 98 — and has raced over today's distance before. His best recent effort is a runner-up three starts back, but the form has since dipped to a third and a fifth, and a 232-day absence adds to the concern.

runners_data.name: Tannery Park
runners_data.note: Lightly raced four-year-old returning from a 409-day absence for Barry Connell with Mark Walsh aboard; won at 22f on good ground and placed twice, but the fade-in-finish flag is a concern over this stamina trip — the layoff is the biggest unknown.
runners_data.comment: Tannery Park was successful last time out but that was 409 days ago, and the two runs before that brought nothing better than 5th. A rating of 94 keeps him around midfield, though the lengthy absence since raises a fitness question.

runners_data.name: Another Glendaars
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist for C Byrnes and J J Slevin, last seen 27 days ago; sim-going record shows 5/6 with no wins or places on good ground, so the surface is a worry despite the fitness edge.
runners_data.comment: Another Glendaars has been a model of consistency without a win, finishing between 4th and 7th in each of his last five starts. A rating of 98 places him mid-pack, with more needed to break through.

runners_data.name: Ballyglass Beauty
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old prominent runner in headgear (p) for Cian Collins; placed twice in 15 good-ground runs and has shown consistency at 23-26f, though OR 93 and recent form of 8442-7 suggest she is just outside the winning picture.
runners_data.comment: Ballyglass Beauty has raced over today's distance before and was runner-up two starts back, racing consistently throughout — form that rates him third in the field at 103, above his official mark of 93. Still without a win, an 8th further back is the main risk.

runners_data.name: Sharetheknowledge
runners_data.note: Prominent-style runner wearing tongue tie, last out 260 days ago for Paul Tobin; placed twice from 11 good-ground attempts over similar trips, but the extended absence and failed jockey booking (no jockey listed) is a red flag.
runners_data.comment: Sharetheknowledge's recent runs have been modest — twice 4th but also pulled up and a 9th — and he's now 260 days without a run, yet he still rates fourth in the field on our figures at 102, well above his official mark of 92.

runners_data.name: The Little Yank
runners_data.note: Eleven-year-old prominent type in a hood, whose recent history is dominated by heavy/soft ground on Irish tracks — five of his last five runs come on HEA or SOF going; good-to-firm conditions here represent a genuine step into unfamiliar territory.
runners_data.comment: The Little Yank has raced over today's distance before and landed one five starts back, though he has been pulled up in every start since — a puzzle to solve. Even so, he rates second in the field on our figures at 104, above his official mark of 92.

runners_data.name: Island Mccoo
runners_data.note: Wearing a tongue tie and in sharp form — won last time at 24f on good ground just 25 days ago for Donncha Duggan; sim-going record of 2 wins and 2 places from 9 good-ground runs makes this one of the most course-conditions-relevant profiles in the field.
runners_data.comment: Island McCoo was successful last time out and was runner-up two starts back too, a pleasing upturn after a pair of 8ths further back. He has raced over today's distance before and a rating of 93 keeps him right in the mix at midfield.

runners_data.name: Knocknagoran Lady
runners_data.note: Ran just 8 days ago and won at 22f on good ground, equipped with tongue tie and visor; trainer Cian Hughes has 0 from 1 in the past 14 days, but the horse's form and quick turnaround suggest confidence — sim-going reads 1W3P from 8 good-ground runs.
runners_data.comment: Knocknagoran Lady landed one last time out, just eight days ago, and was third three starts back too, so she does have a recent win to her name. A rating of 88 leaves her towards the lower half of this field despite that spark of form.

runners_data.name: Georgia Celena
runners_data.note: Prominent-style mare for John C McConnell with apprentice Dylan Kidd claiming 7lbs; trainer has 0 wins from 24 runners in the past 14 days which is a stark stat — 1W5P from 12 good-ground runs at this sort of trip points to a consistent but limited profile.
runners_data.comment: Georgia Celena has been fairly consistent without quite landing one, third last time out and third again five starts back, despite a fall four starts back in between. She has raced over today's distance and going before, though her trainer is currently out of form.

runners_data.name: Love Like This
runners_data.note: Won last time at 24f on good ground 25 days ago for John Patrick Ryan with Brian Barry (7lbs claim); sim-going shows 1W3P from 6 good-ground runs and her prominent style should allow her to track any early tempo — yard has 2 wins from 16 runners in the last 14 days.
runners_data.comment: Love Like This landed one last time out and has been competitive throughout, with runner-up and third-place efforts also among her last six starts. She has raced over today's distance before and a rating of 91 keeps her in the middle of this field.

runners_data.name: Thewaybackhome
runners_data.note: Five-year-old hold-up type with a hood, placed third and fourth in his last two runs; 35 days since last run, sim-going of 3/6 with one place on good ground is moderate — interesting profile at OR 87 but needs the pace to be genuine to get competitive.
runners_data.comment: Thewaybackhome has been solid without a win, 4th last time out and third two starts back, though a 9th further back in the sequence is a blot. A rating of 92 keeps him around midfield, with more needed to force his way into contention.

runners_data.name: Hay Baby
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner for Emmet Mullins returning after 61 days; no wins or places from 4 good-ground runs in the history data — the sim-going record is uninspiring and Mullins has 0 wins from 5 runners in the past fortnight.
runners_data.comment: Hay Baby has been a picture of consistency without a win, finishing between 4th and 6th in four of her last five starts. A rating of 90 places her just outside the midfield bracket, with more needed to threaten.

runners_data.name: Coppola
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott-trained hold-up type who fades in the finish — flagged with that warning and a history of 0W2P from 9 good-ground runs; Elliott's yard is in form (11 wins from 49 in 14 days), but the fade flag and recent pulled-up runs make this hard to trust over 3m1f.
runners_data.comment: Coppola was runner-up in three straight starts but has since been pulled up twice, still without a win in that run. She has raced over today's distance before, and a rating of 87 leaves plenty to find from an outsider's chance.

runners_data.name: Technology
runners_data.note: A natural prominent racer whose OR 84 and STYLE_FIT tag (0.92) reflect that it is unlikely to secure the prominent berth it needs with so many rivals wanting the same ground; recent form includes a fall and a 9th, and sim-going is 0W2P from 13 good-ground starts — hard to fancy.
runners_data.comment: Technology was runner-up four starts back but has since gone backwards, no better than 9th and fell last time out. He has raced over today's distance before and a rating of 92 keeps him in the mix around midfield.

runners_data.name: Go Avel
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse pushed into the midfield map slot due to field congestion at the rear; OR 80 with a fade-in-finish flag and 0W0P from 9 good-ground runs — the STYLE_FIT discount applies and the form offers little encouragement at this trip.
runners_data.comment: Go Avel has struggled to make an impact, no better than 4th and including two 9ths and a pulled-up run in her last four starts, still without a win. A rating of 80 leaves her near the foot of this field.

runners_data.name: Gypsy Poet
runners_data.note: Four-year-old genuine hold-up type similarly displaced on the pace map; last ran 252 days ago for Liz Doyle, sim-going shows 0W0P from 5 good-ground runs and all five recent efforts have been placed 6th or worse — the absence and profile make this extremely difficult to fancy.
runners_data.comment: Gypsy Poet has managed nothing better than 6th in his last five starts and remains without a win, out of the weights at the bottom of our figures. He has raced over today's distance before but a 252-day absence adds another obstacle.

runners_data.name: Whatyouwant
runners_data.note: A front-running type for Gerard Kyne, last out 8 days ago, whose natural style is displaced to midfield by the field's pace congestion; won at 25f on good ground and has 2W2P from 13 good-ground starts, but the STYLE_FIT discount (0.93) must temper any case for it getting a prominent run.
runners_data.comment: Whatyouwant landed one three starts back but has been below that level since, pulled up and a 7th in her last two starts. She has raced over today's distance and going before and a rating of 91 keeps her in the mix at midfield.

runners_data.name: Toor Moon
runners_data.note: Prominent style similarly squeezed by field size and mapped to midfield; OR 72 with recent form of three zeros and an unseated — sim-going shows 0W4P from 10 good-ground runs, and the trainer has 0 from 1 in the last 14 days, so hard to identify a winning angle.
runners_data.comment: A third at the far end of his last five is his one flash of form, but he has been well below that since — a pair of poor efforts and then an unseat last time — and remains without a win. Our 86 rating leaves him towards the rear of this field.

runners_data.name: Strong Contender
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with a tongue tie for Norman Lee, last seen 25 days ago; OR 81 and 0W1P from 4 good-ground runs, with two 13th-place finishes in recent starts — nothing in the profile to suggest competitive claims at this level.
runners_data.comment: Strong Contender was third at the other end of her last five starts but has since found trouble, including a fall and two unplaced efforts. She has raced over today's distance before, though a rating of 82 leaves her near the bottom of this field.

races.paceDynamic: Down Around is the one confirmed front-runner in a field of 19, and with a sustainable gallop forecast on good-to-firm ground at Kilbeggan over 3m1f, they are set to dictate at a controlled tempo from the front. The field is loaded with prominent-style horses — Technology, Whatyouwant, Toor Moon, Ballyglass Beauty, Sharetheknowledge, Island Mccoo, Knocknagoran Lady and Love Like This all want to race prominently, yet only a handful can realistically secure those early positions behind Down Around, meaning several will be shuffled back and forced to race out of role. The hold-up brigade — Tannery Park, Another Glendaars, Thewaybackhome, Coppola and Hay Baby — will find themselves in a naturally compressed midfield rather than enjoying clear daylight at the rear, given the field size and likely bunching over hurdles at this trip. A controlled, single-pacemaker scenario over a stamina trip on good-to-firm ground strongly favours horses that can travel prominently in the early stages and sustain their effort through the final half-mile — genuine stayers with tactical versatility and good-ground form are the primary beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Down Around Controls Unopposed
scenarios.trigger: If Down Around is allowed to dictate an uncontested, measured gallop and the pack fails to apply pressure through the middle stages.
scenarios.body: Down Around, racing prominently at OR 98, sets a sustainable pace that suits a one-run finish and steadily grinds out the contest over the long 3m1f trip; horses with strong good-ground form who track the leader close-up through the final circuit are ideally placed.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Packers Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the glut of prominent types resolves into a competitive front group that sets a genuinely strong gallop and the race is won from the front ranks.
scenarios.body: With multiple horses pressing for prominent berths early, the pace lifts into a true test of stamina that filters out the hold-up horses who find themselves too far back to land a challenge; prominent runners with proven good-to-firm form at this trip are the primary winners.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If Down Around and the front group set a strong enough gallop that genuine hold-up types get a tow into the race and arrive with a sustained late run.
scenarios.body: Tannery Park, unraced for 409 days but with a winning profile in good ground, and Thewaybackhome, who showed solid form last time, would be the main beneficiaries if they find cover and produce a sustained finish from off the pace.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Steadily Run Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses and the field crawls, producing a sprint finish that rewards tactical speed and handling of good-to-firm ground over the final two flights.
scenarios.body: In a falsely-run race the field bunches and the outcome hinges on a dash to the line rather than stamina, which could see a well-handicapped horse from the prominent group that has fresh enough legs produce a burst; however this scenario is the least likely given the field size and the fact that several genuine stayers are entered.

watchPoints.text: Island Mccoo and Knocknagoran Lady both won last time on good ground and are racing back quickly — watch whether they track Down Around prominently from the outset and travel easily, as the runner who does so most fluently is likely to control the race from the second circuit.

The pack of displaced prominent types — Technology, Whatyouwant and Toor Moon — will attempt to push forward from their predicted midfield positions early; if they force an unexpectedly sharp early gallop, the sustainable pace scenario unravels and the hold-up horses gain a tactical advantage.

Tannery Park's 409-day absence is the critical variable for the hold-up scenario — if Mark Walsh settles her quickly and she travels sweetly in rear, she becomes a live danger late, but any sign of rustiness or anxiety early will likely see her fade in the finish as flagged.

Down Around's last run was 232 days ago — despite being the confirmed front-runner, monitor how fluently it jumps the early hurdles and whether it maintains a true gallop through the back straight, as a sluggish reappearance could compress the field and play into the hands of the prominent movers.

Love Like This carries a 7lb claim for Brian Barry and both she and Knocknagoran Lady (also last-time winners) are trained in the John Patrick Ryan yard which has hit 2 wins from 16 runners in the past fortnight — watch for paddock behaviour and early jumping from both as an indicator of yard sharpness.
